correctness.rationale: For uniform π∈S_n, the unordered prefix set S_i of i values is independent of their relative ranks, including the event R_i that position i is the prefix maximum. If j<i, conditional on R_i, π_j is uniform among S_i except its maximum, which necessarily exceeds j, so conditional P(E_j)= [i(n−j)/n−1]/(i−1). Multiplying its difference from (n−j)/n by P(R_i)=1/i gives Cov(R_i,E_j)=−j/[ni(i−1)]. On j=i, P(max S_i≤i)=1/C(n,i), giving diagonal 1/n−1/[iC(n,i)]; for j>i, π_j is independent of the earlier relative prefix rank, so covariance zero; R1 is constant. Summation yields row 1/(2n)−1/[iC(n,i)] (i≥2); it is positive at interior i=2..n−1 for n≥4 and negative final. Summing rows yields Cov(R,X)=(n−1)/(2n)−(1/n)Σ_{k=1}^{n−1}1/C(n−1,k). The binomial reciprocal bound for n≥5 proves strictly positive, while n=2,3,4 give −1/4,−1/6,−1/24; expansion yields 1/2−3/(2n)+O(n^(−2)). Standard independent record ranks and Eulerian X variance yield Corr∼sqrt(3)/sqrt(n log n). Independent literal enumeration of every π for n=2..7 reproduced every matrix entry and global totals −1/4,−1/6,−1/24,1/15,3/20,89/420. Finite checks corroborate an all-n conditional-subset proof.
